title: Nareshiya

paragraphs: Shimon bar Nareshiya is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud at the end of Kilayim 3:1, where Hyman says the name mistakenly appears as Gershiya. He considers it very likely to be the name of the town known as Nareshaa, as in Yoma 69a, Beitzah 15a, Pesachim 107a, Gittin 69b, Bava Metzia 68a, and Chullin 127a.

notes.text: The alleged erroneous spelling is identical to the heading in the supplied text; the intended contrast remains unresolved.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Kilayim3:1 scalar has Shimon bar Narshiya beside Rabbi Ba bar Kahana, in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name. It supports that occurrence, without proving every intermediate link or a different erroneous spelling. Supplied heading and alleged erroneous form are identically נרשיה; earlier machine גרשיה is a discrepancy, not a checked printed variant. The earlier3:4 comparison without bar is inherited, not newly read. Hyman’s very likely town Nareshaa proposal remains at that force and attributed, not a modern geographical identity.

Hyman’s printed page 949 distinguishes Nareshiya (נרשיה) from the form he calls erroneous, Gershiya (גרשיה). The supplied transcription gives Nareshiya twice. The consulted Kilayim 3:1 has Shimon bar Narshiya and 3:4 has Shimon Narshiya without bar, both in the related teaching. Hyman also distinguishes the readings with and without bar on page 1206. The printed Beitzah reference is 15a, where the felt of Neresh is mentioned, while the supplied text has 16a. The other five cited Bavli passages also attest Neresh or a related form. The identification of this name as a place remains Hyman’s very likely suggestion.
